audit.whatIsWrong: Twenty-two fields called Zoe 'he', 'him' or 'his' — tldr, winCon, tradeGood, tradeBad, six phase whys, breakdown.wave, breakdown.trading, four do's/don'ts titles and bodies, and six report entries.
audit.why: champ-gender.js lists Zoe as female, and the owner is addressed as 'you', so every third-person pronoun on the page refers to the enemy.
audit.corrected: Every lint-flagged field is fixed in this proposal; the pronoun-only fixes keep the sentence and length identical.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer rows 0, 3 and 6 disagreed with the content layer and the packet levelChart (full: Zoe / Skill / Skill; content and packet: Orianna / Zoe / Orianna).
audit.why: At level 1 she has neither the bubble nor a charged Paddle Star, so an 815-range ball wins the contact; levels 4-5 are hers because a landed Sleepy Trouble Bubble doubles the waking hit; grouped, a multi-target Shockwave outvalues a single-target pick hunter.
audit.corrected: Full sides moved onto the content/packet verdict on those three rows, with whys and the row-3 rating rewritten. win[] already held the correct tokens.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase whys were generic Orianna boilerplate naming none of her spikes.
audit.why: Her spike is levels 4-5 once the bubble and a levelled Q are both online; Portal Jump only blinks 575 and back, so she never outgrows your R.
audit.corrected: Whys now key to the 18s bubble, the 8.5s redirectable Q and the 575-range blink.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page said what sleep actually does, and the More Sparkles! auto-reset was never mentioned.
audit.why: Sleepy Trouble Bubble reduces the target's magic resist while asleep and the first source of damage that breaks the sleep is doubled up to a cap — which is why buying raw resistances is not the answer and why the bubble, not the Q, is the thing to dodge. More Sparkles! empowers her next basic attack after any cast, so the auto wind-up is the tell that the combo has started. Paddle Star can be redirected in flight, so sidestepping early does not beat it.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[0].d now states the sleep effect, dosFull[0].d states the auto-reset tell, and breakdown.cooldowns carries the redirect.

audit.why: It is the field that holds real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Sleepy Trouble Bubble 18s->14s, Paddle Star 8.5s, Portal Jump down to 5s at 575 range stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.mid claimed protect-ball 'doubles every gank' (lint UNSUPPORTED_MAGNITUDE); dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were tradeGood and tradeBad pasted verbatim.
audit.why: No number supports 'doubles', and neither bullet answered its own title.

notes: This matchup carried the worst pronoun damage in the slice — 22 fields called Zoe 'he/him/his', including the TL;DR and six report entries. All of them are fixed here; the report edits are pronoun-only swaps at identical length, made because the lint flagged them, not as sweep expansion. Full-layer chart rows 0, 3 and 6 disagreed with the content layer and the packet and were moved onto their verdict (win[] already correct). The suspectNames entry for 'Paddle Star' is a false positive: the page writes 'Paddle Star', the kit name is 'Paddle Star!' with the exclamation mark, and the page's usage is correct in prose. One missing-interaction headline I did not act on: 'terrain-cuts-retreat' claims Sleepy Trouble Bubble creates terrain that cuts your retreat, but Riot's description of the ability is drowsy-then-sleep with reduced magic resist and a doubled waking hit, with no terrain in it — the derived terrain flag looks like a tooltip-parsing misfire, so I left that claim out rather than telling a reader to hold Flash for a wall that may not exist.
